A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Foveated Reasoner study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison after matching pagination and citation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, training and inference ablations, supervision comparisons, and qualitative analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds localization-quality and end-to-end efficiency measurements in Section 4.3, Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: The stateful decoding procedure, continuous foveation head, coldstart training, GRPO objectives, and region regularization are retained. Appendix Algorithms A1–A2 are unchanged; coordinate-symbol and sentence-index edits do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Training still uses Visual CoT, RefCOCO/+/g, and ScienceQA; evaluation retains the 12 Visual CoT datasets and V* Bench. The new localization and efficiency analyses use existing datasets without introducing new task requirements or input scenarios.

E2.justification: The new analyses introduce explicit comparator controls: VisCoT7B for localization, and VisCoT7B plus original-resolution Qwen2.5-VL3B for runtime. These reuse existing baseline families in new comparisons; comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds coverage and IoU@0.5 evaluation on four existing datasets, plus single-H100 profiling on V7W using tokenization-to-prediction latency, peak VRAM, and throughput. These are additional evaluation protocols; the earlier splits, training budgets, and benchmark scoring settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds substantive tests of two central questions: whether foveations capture annotated evidence, and whether token savings translate into practical computational savings. Tables 5–6 also compare reasoning and no-reasoning variants. These extend the earlier accuracy/token-budget ablations with localization diagnostics and direct system profiling.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same mean and standard deviation reporting for visual-token counts. The new tables provide point estimates without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Previously unreported localization and computational results substantially extend the evidence. Table 5 reports V7W coverage of 8.1% versus 63.3%, but IoU@0.5 of 27.8 versus 18.5, for VisCoT7B versus reasoning-enabled FoveateR3B. Table 6 adds latencies of 9.78 seconds for VisCoT7B and 1.06/2.62 seconds for FoveateR3B without/with reasoning. Earlier result entries are unchanged; these are new comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 introduces the definition of cumulative GT-region coverage as the fraction of ground-truth pixels covered by the union of predicted boxes. This is a limited addition to the mathematical evaluation quantities; the POMDP formulation, Proposition 1 and its proof, and training derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about stateful single-pass foveation, non-linguistic actions, learning without human-annotated foveation trajectories, and accuracy under restricted visual-token budgets. The new experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 explains why cumulative coverage accommodates recovery across multiple foveations, attributes runtime savings to avoiding repeated encoding, and interprets reasoning overhead as evidence for additional costs in text-grounded methods. That last comparison is an extrapolation rather than a direct measurement. Appendix C's substantive limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The added efficiency experiment documents its single-H100 hardware, timing boundary, and throughput definition. Existing architecture details, hyperparameters, training times, prompts, pseudocode, and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds ERGO to the references and expands the positioning of already-cited visual-focusing work, including ZoomEye and VisionThink. Section 5 adds an explicit four-part contrast with prior approaches. Most citation changes are renumbering; ERGO is not added as an evaluated baseline.

P1.justification: v2 inserts Section 4.3, expands the visual-focusing discussion in related work, and makes localized grammar, notation, and explanatory edits. The overall narrative order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 5–6 are added, Table 1 gains asterisks on the previously identified zero-shot datasets, and Table 3's caption clarifies the oracle. Existing figures and appendix displays are retained, with subsequent material reflowing around the additions.

improvement.justification: v1 supported efficiency mainly through visual-token counts; v2 adds direct runtime, memory, and throughput measurements alongside localization diagnostics, strengthening the empirical support for its central rationale. The improvement is limited by profiling only V7W, comparing unequal backbone sizes, and extrapolating overhead to text-grounded methods without directly timing them. The earlier scientific content and reproducibility material are preserved.
